edit.description: gate_installed (~561-609) runs evaluate_placements as a dry run and tallies ANY placement entry whose outcome isn't Unchanged into the per-kind hook/guard/post_tool_use flags that drive the `install.gate-installed` finding. b7b2a7a6 added `ApplyOutcome::SupersededByMember` (drift.rs:2518) for exactly the case where a synthesized hook placement is correctly superseded by an authored `hook` kind member — but gate_installed was never updated to treat it like Unchanged, so `check` now flags that correctly-authored hook forever, the same false positive `install`'s own render just stopped showing. Exclude SupersededByMember from the tally alongside Unchanged.

b7b2a7a6 shipped with no test at all for detect_hook_member_conflicts/SupersededByMember (only a trailing-newline diff landed in this file). Add one exercising install::run with an authored hook member superseding a synthesized placement (pattern at ~581, ~825): install's render names `superseded-by-member`, and gate_installed/`check` report no finding for it.

summary: gate_installed still tallies the new SupersededByMember outcome as needing install, so check flags a correctly-authored hook member forever — the false positive moved, not fixed.

per.section: The placements and their enforcement modes

tests.asserts: an authored hook member superseding a synthesized placement reports no install.gate-installed finding at check, and no test previously exercised this path at all

acceptance: A harness whose authored `hook` kind member supersedes a synthesized placement (SessionStart/guard/post-tool-use) reports no `install.gate-installed` finding, matching install's own SupersededByMember render; a regression exercises install::run with a real superseding hook member.
notes: observed at bf4b4168 (cascade audit of INSTALL-HOOK-PLACEMENT-FALSE-APPLIED's amendments 3-4), re-verified after that entry shipped (b7b2a7a6/bd10edd1 on disk): gate_installed was not touched by the fix, and no regression test exists for the new outcome at all. scoped at bd10edd1

edit.description: emit_one's banner branch (~2338-2348, added by bccf42c0's move from install to emit) only places the managed-projection banner, and only for a frontmatterless markdown projection (`projection.fields.is_empty()`). It never places the frontmatter `#` note — only install.rs's project_note (~1925) does, and only when frontmatter already exists. Since emit owns a represented projection's bytes in full (pipeline.md "Emit"; no file is part-authored, part-emitted), extend emit to place the note too for any markdown projection that carries frontmatter, so a freshly emitted projection needs no separate `install` run to converge its note.

Narrow project_note's/evaluate_placements's role to converging drift on an already-emit-owned projection's existing note wording, rather than being the sole originator for a fresh one — the same narrowing bccf42c0 already did for the banner.

Regression: deleting a built-in skill's SKILL.md (or any frontmatter-bearing modeled projection) then running `emit` alone produces a projection carrying its note; `check`'s gate_installed (src/install.rs:561) reports no install.gate-installed finding without a separate `install` run.

summary: emit places the managed-projection banner but never the frontmatter note, so every freshly emitted projection with frontmatter reports install.gate-installed until install runs separately.

tests.asserts: a freshly emitted frontmatter-bearing projection carries its note without a separate install run, and check reports no missing-note finding for it

acceptance: A markdown projection with frontmatter, freshly emitted with no prior install run, carries both its managed-projection banner (where applicable) and its frontmatter note; check's gate_installed reports no finding for it.
notes: observed at bf4b4168 (GH #57). bccf42c0 moved banner placement from install to emit but left the note behind — the part-authored/part-emitted gap invariant 7 forbids, for the note instead of the banner. Subtraction candidate rides along: once emit places both, install's note placement over emit-owned projections is a duplicate to retire — name it in the shipping commit body. Chained on drift.rs/install.rs collisions with the guard/install cluster. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Severity (~19) is a closed two-value enum (Error, Warn); Diagnostic (~35) carries no way to mark a warn-severity finding as disclosure rather than a dialable advisory violation. Add the distinction — a third Severity variant, or a `note`/non-violation flag on Diagnostic — that `--deny-advisories` treats as never-blocking while every reporter still prints it.

check (~49) pushes the `coverage.checked` per-kind summary unconditionally at warn severity (its own doc comment: "Returns warn-severity diagnostics only"). Mark it with the new non-violation distinction — it is disclosure (what was checked), never a violation a corpus could tune.

The `--deny-advisories` exit-flip (~250-256) currently promotes ANY warn-severity diagnostic to blocking; it must skip the new non-violation marker so a clean harness's own coverage.checked note never trips it.
New case: a clean represented harness (no contract violations) run with `--deny-advisories` exits zero, though `coverage.checked` is present in the output — the case no existing test asserts.

Every reporter renders Severity by matching all its variants — add the new non-violation variant/flag to each match arm so it still prints (disclosure, never suppressed) rather than failing to compile or silently dropping the note.
The shared test harness helper constructs Diagnostic/Severity values other test files reuse; widen it for the new variant so dependent tests keep compiling.
Existing assertions pin coverage.checked's severity as plain `warn` — update them to assert the new non-violation marker instead.

summary: check --deny-advisories can never pass: the coverage.checked disclosure note is pushed at warn severity unconditionally, and --deny-advisories treats any warn as a blocking violation.

tests.asserts: a clean harness with `check --deny-advisories` exits zero even though the coverage.checked summary is present in the diagnostics

acceptance: `--deny-advisories` promotes only real advisory violations to blocking, never the coverage.checked disclosure note; a clean represented harness exits zero under it.
notes: observed at e1b26728 (cascade GH #42). Intent invariant 5: a shipped coverage clause enters advisory so it is dialable, not so it blocks CI — coverage.checked is disclosure, never a violation. Widened at fb89f675 (gate-revert 1 of 2: a new Severity variant ripples to every renderer and the shared test helper) — files[] now states the ripple up front. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Declaration rows for a layout source come from exactly two paths: emit over the program's declared members (drift.rs derive_layout_rows) and check's read-time derivation for local-locus kinds only (compose.rs local_document_rows). A discovered committed member of a layout kind that the program never declares is read at check for its field slots (compose.rs layout_unit) and for nothing else: coverage prints `invariant (0)`, explain says "Nested members: none", every leaf address fails, and no finding names the cause. Add a finding, advisory (config.stale posture), when a discovered committed layout-kind member has no matching provenance row in the lock — naming the two remedies: declare it in the program and re-emit, or declare the kind local.
The new finding sits beside config_stale (~2643) — the freshness-fact family the gate already reads disk-vs-lock through — rather than a second comparison mechanism.

Regression: a committed layout-kind document discovery finds but the program's member list omits produces the new advisory finding naming the file and remedy, rather than reading as zero coverage with no explanation.

summary: A committed layout document discovery finds but the program never declares yields no declaration rows anywhere — coverage, explain, and leaf addresses all read silently empty, no finding names why.

tests.asserts: a discovered committed member of a layout kind with no provenance row in the lock surfaces an advisory finding naming the file and the remedy, instead of reading as silent zero coverage

acceptance: check reports a discovered layout-kind member absent from the lock's declaration rows as a named advisory finding; the pipeline.md split (the gate reads declarations from the lock family and nowhere else, local locus excepted) stays intact — the fix is the finding, not new read-time derivation for committed sources.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb, re-filed at d760aa04 (cascade F10, GH #43 as retitled; drained by plan tick ab4a3ead with no entry — re-filed verbatim, now routed). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: read_layout_document (~1959, the one reader both emit's committed lowering and check's local-locus derivation share) lowers a Layout::read into LayoutDocumentRows carrying only `nested` and `satisfies` — the verbatim prose region's own span (LayoutReading::prose) and field-section spans are read but never become a row. A layout declaring `prose` after a `collection`/`field` region (a legal, non-first position for the one verbatim prose region) still has the document's leading preamble land there (preamble_taken in layout.rs ~146), with no row or explain surface ever naming which region actually captured it or what it captured.

explain's per-member narration has nothing to read for a layout's prose region span; wire the new row (or feature) in so a layout member's prose content is addressable/visible the same way its fields and members already are.

Regression: a layout with a prose region declared after a collection region still binds the document's preamble to it (existing behavior, per 0019's preamble-or-import rule), and the captured span is now visible via a leaf/row `explain` and the lock can address, not silently dropped.

summary: A layout's verbatim prose region span is read but never becomes a lock row or reaches explain, so an author can't see which region captured the preamble or what it captured.

tests.asserts: a layout's verbatim prose region span reaches an addressable row/leaf, visible to explain, matching how field and collection regions already surface

acceptance: A layout document's verbatim prose region content reaches a row or projection explain can narrate, instead of being read by Layout::read and then dropped on the floor by every downstream consumer.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb, re-filed at d760aa04 (cascade F10 refinement, GH #43). Distinct from LAYOUT-DUPLICATE-PROSE-REGION-REFUSAL (refuses a second prose region at admissibility) and LAYOUT-COLLECTION-MEMBER-OWN-SPAN-LEAF (a collection member's own span) — this is the top-level prose region's own visibility gap. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: target_identity (~1593) keys an edge target on a bare `(kind, identity)` pair, splitting `target` on its first `:` — it has no path to accept representation.md's own nested-member address grammar (`<host-address>/<kind>/<key>`). Parse the full address grammar here (host-qualified and bare short forms both), so `resolved_edges` (~1252) and its dangling-diagnostic path both carry the parsed host-qualified identity through to findings.

EdgeField (~55)'s `to` is a target-kind set only; an edge field's entries are free-text addresses at the instance, so the SDK itself needs no schema change — confirm this at scoping and note if a validator narrows what an entry may spell.

explain's edge/finding narration prints a resolved or dangling target's identity; once target_identity carries the parsed host-qualified form, the printed address should show it rather than the bare short form alone.

Regression: two same-keyed nested members under different hosts are each addressable from an edge field via the full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` form, resolving to the correct one rather than forcing a rename.

summary: An edge field can't spell a nested target's full host-qualified address — only the bare (kind, identity) short form — so two same-keyed nested members force a rename instead of an address.

tests.asserts: an edge field entry spelling `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` resolves to that exact nested member, alongside the existing bare `kind:identity` short form

acceptance: target_identity parses the full nested address grammar per representation.md's member section, resolving both bare and host-qualified spellings; explain and findings print the resolved form; the duplicate-key admissibility refusal (NESTED-MEMBER-DUPLICATE-KEY-ADMISSIBILITY) stays the resolver's bar, not the address itself.
notes: observed at f8344d20 (session, plan's 0049 spec-delta pass narrowing its own prior routing). 0049's Decision names every verb accepting one address grammar; its Rejected bullet turns down corpus-unique keys as the address itself. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Audit every admissibility diagnostic's message text — e.g. clause_collision_diagnostics (~167, message ~184-189 names only the shared label) — so each names the concrete edit (which two clauses/members collided and the argument that discriminates them) rather than restating lock/contract state alone.
Audit diagnostic construction call sites for the same bar where messages are assembled rather than authored at the diagnostic definition.

summary: Audit admissibility refusal messages so each names the concrete edit an author would make, never only the lock state.

tests.asserts: admissibility refusal messages name the discriminating edit, not just the lock state

acceptance: Every admissibility refusal message names the edit an author would make — the colliding clauses/members and their discriminator — never the lock state alone.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (John, 09-05 redirect, entry 3 of 4); narrowed at bf4b4168, item d: the read.rs/narrate_kind item targeted narration that doesn't exist (narrate_kind prints guidance/cite only) — that half collapses, since LAYOUT-LOUD-READ-SWALLOWED-REGION's new LayoutError message now carries the region-naming bar directly. Chained behind LAYOUT-DUPLICATE-PROSE-REGION-REFUSAL and NESTED-MEMBER-DUPLICATE-KEY-ADMISSIBILITY (shared src/admissibility.rs). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: resolve's explicit `kind:` prefix branch (~221-224: `target.strip_prefix("kind:")` unconditionally returns `Species::Kind(name)`) has no existence check — unlike the bare-name fallthrough a few lines below, which already gates on `contracts.contains_key(target)`. Fold in the same check so an undeclared qualified kind name is NotFound (GH #47), rather than narrate_kind (476) reporting 'no guidance declared' identically for a declared-but-unguided kind and an undeclared one. Then extend narrate_kind: `Contract` (contract.rs:24) carries only name/clauses/guidance — no regions or templates — so a layout kind's regions and a composed kind's admitted embedded kinds must be narrated from whatever data the engine already populates for them (declarations.layouts / declarations.nested_members); define what 'composed kind' means here or drop the term.

Regression: explain kind:<undeclared-name> reads NotFound; explain kind:<layout-kind> prints its regions and a fitting skeleton; explain kind:<composed-host-kind> prints its admitted embedded kinds and leaves.

summary: Make explain kind:<x> the adopter's authoring entry point: NotFound for an undeclared kind, a skeleton for a layout kind, admitted embedded kinds for a composed kind.

tests.asserts: explain kind:<x> is the adopter's authoring entry point for every kind shape, and NotFound for an undeclared name

acceptance: explain kind:<x> resolves NotFound for a name no kind declares; for a layout kind it narrates the regions in order plus a skeleton document; for a composed kind it narrates the admitted embedded kinds and their leaves.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (John, 09-05 redirect, entry 4 of 4; GH #47 folded in); corrected at bf4b4168 (cascade-integrations audit, item e): the unchecked path is the explicit `kind:` prefix branch, not a 'bare-name fallthrough' (that path already checks existence). Chained behind EXPLAIN-KIND-QUALIFIED-ADDRESS-FORM per audit item (f) — both reshape resolve's qualifier grammar and share src/read.rs/tests/read_verbs.rs; land the one-grammar tokenizer first. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: New well-formedness check beside nested_member_admissibility (~60-79, the real neighbor — not satisfies_label_admissibility, which judges a different, host-blind ambiguity): a single host declaring the SAME (kind, key) nested member twice is a malformed lock, refused at admissibility. Two DIFFERENT hosts sharing a (kind, key) are NOT coincident under 0049's grammar (`spec:alpha/invariant/x` and `spec:beta/invariant/x` are distinct addresses) — that case is a resolution-time ambiguity, not an admissibility refusal; see graph.rs below.

resolves (~1609) is a boolean `.any()` over `by_kind`'s pooled Vec (compose::embedded_features_by_kind, ~1138, pushes every host's rows into one shared per-kind Vec with no host on the Features) — a duplicate (kind, key) across hosts today resolves to whichever matches first, silently. When a BARE (unqualified) target or explain name matches more than one nested member of a kind across different hosts, refuse at resolution (a new graph.route finding) naming every colliding host — the full host-qualified address (GRAPH-EDGE-TARGET-HOST-QUALIFIED-ADDRESS's grammar) always resolves unambiguously. Requires threading `host` onto Features/the graph Node — compose::embedded_member_features (~1194) currently drops `row.host` when lifting `id: row.key.clone()` (~1204).
explain's bare-name resolution needs the same ambiguity refusal as graph.route, naming every host a bare/explain name could mean.

Two regressions: (1) one host declaring the same (kind, key) nested member twice refuses at admissibility; (2) two different hosts each declaring a same-kind-same-key nested member: a bare/explain-name reference to that key refuses at resolution naming both hosts, while either host's full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` address always resolves.

summary: A duplicate (kind, key) nested member is coincident only within one host; across hosts a bare address is ambiguous at resolution, never silently picked.

tests.asserts: same-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses at admissibility; cross-host duplicate (kind, key) refuses only a bare/unqualified reference, at resolution, naming both hosts

acceptance: A host repeating its own (kind, key) nested member refuses loud at admissibility. Two different hosts sharing a (kind, key) are legal (distinct addresses per 0049); a bare or explain-name reference ambiguous between them refuses at resolution naming every host, while the full host-qualified address to either always resolves.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (GH #51 half); corrected at bf4b4168: refusing every cross-host duplicate as coincident hard-codes the alternative Decision 0049 rejects — two hosts' same-keyed members are distinct addresses. Neighbor misnamed (satisfies_label_admissibility, not nested_member_admissibility); resolves is host-blind .any(). Chained on GRAPH-EDGE-TARGET-HOST-QUALIFIED-ADDRESS and LAYOUT-DUPLICATE-PROSE-REGION-REFUSAL. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: memberTable (~700-709) indexes top-level composed members by `kind:key`, last-wins for registration rows (intentional, kept as-is per c054dbce — multiple matcher groups on one hook event legitimately share a key). edgeTargetFacts (~255-270), called unconditionally from resolveMemberLeaves (~307) for every embedded value with an edge field, throws when the target is an embedded value elsewhere: at ~270 any `:`-bearing leaf is treated as a whole lookup key, so a host-qualified address (which contains `/`) is never even attempted. Add a SECOND bare-key index for embedded/nested values keyed by `kind:key`, refusing a duplicate bare key across hosts via the same throwing mechanism `uniqueMap` (~233-241) already uses elsewhere — never memberTable's registration-row last-wins, which is a different, intentional case. Also index the full `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` spelling; never treat a bare `kind:key` string as the whole key once it also contains `/` (0049 Rejected: no third address form). Before calling isProjected (~604-606, false for an embedded locus) or projectionPath (~206-213, throws on one), branch: an embedded target derives its path via `projectionPath(host)` instead. Widen the table's resolved-value type — a nested target is an `EmbeddedMemberValue` (kind.ts:376), not a `Member` (kind.ts:223).

Regression: an embedded value's edge field naming another host's embedded value — by bare `kind:key` and by full host-qualified address — resolves target facts and renders, rather than throwing 'resolves to no composed member'.

The existing dangling-target test (~292, `rule:ghost` → /resolves to no composed member/) and the registration-target test (~298, `hook:PreToolUse` → /owns no projection to reference/) both narrow to true-absence and registration-member cases only, now that an embedded-locus target resolves instead of throwing.

summary: A render hook cannot cite a nested member by its bare or host-qualified key: edgeTargetFacts throws on an embedded value naming another host's embedded value.

tests.asserts: an edge field on an embedded value naming a nested (non-top-level) target resolves and renders, by both bare-unique key and full host-qualified address

acceptance: A render hook on an embedded value whose edge field targets another host's embedded value resolves that target's engine-derived facts (name, address, kind, projection path) and renders, instead of emit refusing outright. Scoped to the SDK's own rendering path for bare-unique keys and the host-qualified spelling end-to-end at emit; full nested-address resolution at `check` (graph::target_identity has no `/` grammar; embedded_member_features is host-blind) stays out of scope, tracked by GRAPH-EDGE-TARGET-HOST-QUALIFIED-ADDRESS / NESTED-MEMBER-DUPLICATE-KEY-ADMISSIBILITY.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe F9/F13, GH #50 widened); corrected/widened at bf4b4168 (session, verified by cascade-integrations): items (5)-(7) — index both spellings via the refusing uniqueMap path (never memberTable's intentional registration-row last-wins), fix the isProjected/projectionPath branch order, widen the value type, and scope check-side resolution out. Chained behind KIND-REGISTRATION-EMPTY-EMBEDDED-TYPE (shares sdk/test/emit.test.ts). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: clause_label (84-91) computes `owner.chain(predicate).chain(field).join(".")` — it never reads a row's `section` (heading+marker) or `sections` (require_sections' list) columns, only `field`. Since declarations.ts never sets `field` for either predicate (it stays `None`), EVERY section_contains clause on a kind compiles to `<kind>.section_contains` and every require_sections clause to `<kind>.require_sections` — both predicates collide, not just section_contains's marker. Fold the section_contains row's heading+marker, and the require_sections row's sections list, into the label's discriminating segment when `field` is absent.

stamp_clause_label (1573-1578) is the sole caller of clause_label and passes only `row.field.as_deref()` — it needs the row's `section`/`sections` data threaded through too so the label fix above has something to read.

The existing label-collision test (a_lock_carrying_two_rows_under_one_label_fails_admissibility_loud, ~2907) proves the refusal only on a hand-written lock (via common::clause/write_lock), never through the SDK — which is why this collision was never caught. Add a regression that authors two section_contains clauses (and/or two require_sections clauses) with the actual SDK, compiled through it (reuse the wire_sdk_harness pattern from tests/emit.rs:1748), and asserts the resulting lock carries two distinct labels.

summary: A section_contains/require_sections clause's compiled label never carries its heading/marker/sections, so every clause of that predicate on one kind folds to one label.

tests.asserts: two section_contains (or require_sections) clauses on one kind, compiled through the real SDK, produce two distinct compiled labels and both gate independently

acceptance: An author can declare 'every invariant carries a Test' and '... a Standard' as two independent section_contains clauses on one kind without them folding into one malformed-lock label; the same holds for two require_sections clauses.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade probe, GH #48); corrected at bf4b4168 (session, verified by cascade-integrations): the entry as first filed claimed only the marker drops (heading kept) — wrong on both counts. `field` is undefined for section_contains AND require_sections rows alike (declarations.ts never sets it for either); `section` (heading+marker) IS present in the row but simply never read by clause_label/stamp_clause_label. scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: read_collection_member (222) takes a LayoutMember's leaves from its immediate sub-headings only, keyed by slug; the paragraph directly under the member's own heading lands nowhere. Land it under whichever reserved leaf key `(layout-own-span-leaf)` rules — composed leaves are author-named (NestedMemberRow.leaves keyed by field name, no reserved own-span key exists there; the SDK's `FRAMEWORK_KEYS`/kind.ts:245 `prose` is a member-level value, not a leaf-name reservation). Hazards the fork must rule on: node.body includes sub-heading text (the own span must cut at the first child heading), and a sub-heading slugged to the reserved name would collide with it.
Regression: a layout collection member whose body is `### Title` + a paragraph + `**Test.** ...` (no sub-headings) materializes a non-empty leaves map carrying the paragraph under the ruled key.

summary: A layout collection member's own paragraph span lands nowhere — not a leaf, not the lock, not explain — while its sub-headings' spans do.

tests.asserts: a layout collection member's own span (the text directly under its heading) lands in its leaves, under the ruled reserved key

acceptance: A layout collection member's own paragraph (not just its sub-headings) reaches a leaf, addressable and visible to leaf predicates, leaf addresses, and explain, matching the composed half's full-leaves behavior.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F11, GH #43 leaves gap); corrected at bf4b4168 (cascade-integrations audit, item c): 'the composed half already names it prose' is false — no reserved own-span leaf name exists anywhere in the corpus today. Reserving one is a Decision (John's), tracked by new fork `layout-own-span-leaf`; this entry waits on it. Chained behind LAYOUT-DUPLICATE-PROSE-REGION-REFUSAL (shares src/layout.rs + tests/layout_kind.rs). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: Add `relocate(base, delta)` beside the existing `kind()` factory (~336), so a consumer can extend a built-in kind's facts (e.g. add an edgeField to `rule`, which must stay at .claude/rules to load) without an `as any` cast that silently drops the fact. Mark the produced facts with a relocation marker (e.g. `facts.relocates`) so KINDS-IN-PLAY-NAME-COLLISION-REFUSAL can later tell a legitimate relocation from a genuine name collision.
SDK-side payload assertion: a relocated `rule` kind declaring an added edgeField emits the fact in its compiled declarations (no `as any`, no dropped field).

Rust regression: the emitted edge fact from a relocated built-in resolves a real graph.route edge — proving no engine change is needed, since edges are always read from assembly `edge` rows keyed by `from` kind (never carried on a kind row itself); `graph.route` isn't assertable from an SDK test, hence the split.

summary: A built-in kind cannot take an added edge field; the SDK has no sanctioned relocation constructor and an as any cast drops the edge fact silently.

tests.asserts: a relocated built-in kind's added edge field is emitted, not silently dropped by an as any cast

acceptance: A corpus can add an edge field to a built-in kind (e.g. rule) via the sanctioned relocation form and have it resolve a real graph edge, checked at check and rendered at emit — no as any cast needed. No engine change required: overlay_builtin_kind (compose.rs:453) never needs to carry edgeFields, since edges never live on a kind row.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F13(b), GH #54); reworded at bf4b4168 (cascade-integrations audit, item g): dropped the compose.rs 'extend overlay_builtin_kind' item as unnecessary — edges resolve from assembly edge rows already, regardless of kind-row overlay. relocate() belongs in kind.ts beside kind(), not builtins.ts. Chained behind KIND-REGISTRATION-EMPTY-EMBEDDED-TYPE (shares sdk/src/kind.ts + sdk/test/builtins.test.ts). scoped at bf4b4168

edit.description: kindsInPlay's `admit` closure (~351-355) is first-wins by name — `if (byName.has(facts.name)) return;` — walking harness.members in authored order, so a corpus kind reusing a built-in's name at a different root is silently discarded before it ever reaches the engine's own kind.admissibility check (admissibility.rs:126, joined_kind_admissibility:484 — which already refuses a diverging same-name row, but only once one reaches the lock). Change `admit` to compare the two KindFacts values and refuse a divergence, naming both loci — except when the second carries BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS's relocation marker (`facts.relocates`), which this must recognize and allow.

Regression via the harness's compile path (compileDeclarations): a harness declaring a corpus kind under a built-in's exact name at a different root refuses at load, naming both loci; the sanctioned relocation form still passes.

summary: A corpus kind reusing a built-in's name at a different root is silently discarded by kindsInPlay's first-wins-by-name, with no diagnostic anywhere.

tests.asserts: two distinct KindFacts values sharing one name refuse at load unless one is the sanctioned relocation of the other

acceptance: Declaring a corpus kind that reuses a built-in's name at a different root refuses loud, naming both loci, unless authored through the sanctioned relocation form.
notes: observed at ad10e8cb (cascade F13(c), GH #53); corrected at bf4b4168, item h: the engine already refuses a diverging same-name row once it reaches the lock — the gap is kindsInPlay's SDK-side first-wins discarding the second kind first. `admit` is a closure inside kindsInPlay, not a standalone export. Blocked on BUILTIN-KIND-RELOCATION-EDGE-FIELDS defining the relocation marker this refusal must recognize. scoped at bf4b4168

gate.reason: An idea, not a defect (the raw note's own framing) — a `handle` fact on a target kind has no named consumer today, and the containment-selection family (open question) is the higher-priority extension to this same render-branching surface. Revive when a render hook wants a spelling the closed target-fact set (name, address, kind, projection path) can't already express cleanly.

edit.description: Anticipated: a `handle` fact on KindFacts, read by a render hook branching on target.kind, alongside the existing closed engine-derived target-fact set.

summary: A kind-declared citable handle ('how a reference to a member of this kind reads') — a lower-priority idea, not a defect, with no consumer yet.
acceptance: A kind declaring `handle` lets a reference render hook spell a member of that kind without hand-rolling the branch on target.kind — provable once a real render hook wants one.
